connections.why: The particle model explains why energy input changes state without changing temperature
Moving particles colliding with surfaces is the cause of gas pressure
Newton's laws relate the forces on an object to how its motion changes
Resultant force and momentum underpin springs, levers and collisions
Work done is force multiplied by distance, transferring energy
Internal energy and heat capacity link the particle model to energy stores
Power is the rate of energy transfer; efficiency measures useful output
Moving charge from static electricity is what a current in a circuit is
Electrical power describes how quickly circuits transfer energy
A current creates a magnetic field, the basis of the motor effect
Field patterns explain how electromagnets and motors are built
The motor effect is a force on a current-carrying wire in a field
Mechanical waves travel as oscillations of the particles of matter
Waves transfer energy from one place to another without moving matter
The wave equation and properties apply across the whole EM spectrum
Reflection, refraction and absorption depend on wavelength and medium
Atomic structure explains isotopes and the origin of nuclear radiation
Decay type and penetration determine medical uses and safety risks
Fission and fusion release nuclear energy from changes in mass
Momentum and braking forces explain stopping distances and road safety
Energy resources and efficiency drive the choice of power generation
Generators and transformers move electricity across the National Grid
Gravity provides the centripetal force that keeps satellites in orbit
Circuit measurements are core required practical investigations
Investigating motion and forces develops core scientific skills
